Hiding complexity behind an interface so that higher-level reasoning can proceed without knowledge of lower-level details.
Abstraction works in layers: each level exposes a simplified model and conceals its implementation beneath it.
1. A function abstracts a sequence of steps.
2. A module abstracts a set of functions.
3. An API abstracts an entire system.
Interface vs. implementation: the caller sees what something does; the abstraction decides how.
Information hiding: irrelevant detail is suppressed, not just renamed.
Composability: abstractions can be stacked — each layer need only understand the one immediately below it.
Abstraction makes Declarative programming possible: to declare what should happen, there must be a layer that handles how.
Imperative code is often the implementation layer that a good abstraction hides.
An abstraction leaks when hidden implementation details escape into the interface — forcing callers to know things the abstraction was supposed to conceal.

Abundance is a condition in which people can obtain enough of the goods, services, infrastructure, and opportunities needed to live and act well. In politics, an abundance agenda asks how institutions can make essential things easier to build and provide.

The word names both a material condition and a political project. A promise of abundance is not evidence that a technology will make every scarce resource plentiful or that its benefits will reach everyone.

Greater productive capacity can make some goods cheaper or more accessible. Housing, energy, health care, transportation, and scientific discovery each depend on distinct technologies, institutions, and constraints.
Lower costs can increase demand. describes cases where improved efficiency makes a resource cheaper to use and total use rises, potentially offsetting some expected savings.

More supply can ease prices in the market where supply expands, but a technology's productivity gains do not automatically reduce every price. Demand, bottlenecks, market power, and distribution shape who benefits.

A local wealth shock can raise bids for a scarce asset such as housing even while another sector experiences falling production costs. Those effects can coexist; neither alone describes the overall price level.

Slopsquatting is a modern supply-chain threat in AI-powered workflows, where coding agents can hallucinate non-existent but plausible package names that malicious actors can use to deliver malware.
Slopsquatting: When AI Agents Hallucinate Malicious Packages | Trend Micro (US)

Slopsquatting is an evolution of the classic typosquatting attack. Rather than relying on human typographical errors however, attackers exploit AI-generated hallucinations instead. When a coding agent hallucinates a dependency—such as starlette-reverse-proxy—an attacker can publish a malicious package under that exact name. Developers who unwittingly run the generated installation commands may inadvertently download and execute malware.

What is fait accompli and amor fati, how are these related if at all, and why are more and more podcasts related to Agentic Engineering talking about these term

Short answer: Fait accompli is a French phrase for an irreversible done deal — something already decided or executed, so later objection is mostly theater. Amor fati is Latin for "love of fate" — a Stoic / Nietzschean stance of actively affirming what has happened (and what you cannot control), not merely enduring it. They are related as situation vs stance: a fait accompli is the irreversible fact; amor fati is one response to living with irreversible facts. Agentic-engineering discourse leans on both because agents keep producing irreversible outcomes faster than humans can deliberate, and the cultural shock of that speed needs a vocabulary for both the done deal and how to live with it.

LangGraph is LangChain's low-level orchestration framework designed for building stateful, long-running agent workflows. It was widely adopted in enterprise agent architectures by October 2025 and has become the backbone for complex LangChain-based applications where durability and replayable state are required.

Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK was released in mid-2025 to support safe and structured multi-agent development around Claude 3.5 and its successors. It focuses on tool use, managed environments, and safety-first agent deployment.

AgentKit, introduced at OpenAI's 2025 DevDay, is an end-to-end agent development framework featuring built-in deployment, evaluation, and UI tools. Despite being relatively new, it quickly gained traction and reflects strong adoption among OpenAI API users.
